correctness.rationale: For fixed rank-2r A and B of rank t, kernel equations prove rank [A,B;-B^T,0]=2(t+j), where 2j is the restricted rank of A on ker B^T. Isotropic radicals and symplectic quotient counts give the stated finite Gaussian transfer, with exact invalid-index conventions. Rectangular matrix rank counts give the complete tripartite specialization. Finite-field exact character-count conversion uses the standard class-two odd-characteristic orbit method. Standalone exhaustive weighted-matrix checks (including all 531441 K_(2,2,2) assignments over F3, and characteristic-two and GF4 cases) agree; no finite check is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nontrivial claim is an explicit rank-law universal under joining an arbitrary graph to more than one mutually nonadjacent vertex and the resulting K_(a,b,c), a,b,c>=2 character-degree census. Related single-vertex coning, trees, cycles, classical symplectic restrictions, and orbit-method reductions are explicitly excluded as novelty. Full primary-text comparisons with Mainkar, O’Brien–Voll, Rossmann, and Lewis et al., together with published-finding corpus semantic comparisons, found no direct statement or demonstrated dominating implication. Historical priority remains provisional.
